source.title: Transient beta activity and cortico-muscular connectivity during sustained motor behaviour

confidence_rationale: Direct MEG+EMG empirical test (n=18) of whether beta activity/connectivity is sustained when a motor state is sustained. It is NOT: even during continuous isometric gripping, motor beta and cortico-muscular coupling occurred as short transient bursts, and sustained demand did not prolong beta-event duration. This qualifies MECH-445's 'beta coupling elevation' reading: a closure-driven latch elevation is unlikely to be a tonic beta level and must instead be cashed out as elevated burst RATE / coupling probability. Mixed rather than weakens, because the finding is fully compatible with a burst-rate implementation of the same mechanism -- it refutes only the naive tonic-maintenance reading.
failure_signatures: Motor beta and cortico-muscular beta connectivity were transient (short bursts) even when motor behaviour was sustained -- a tonic 'beta latch held high for the duration of commitment' reading of MECH-445 is not supported by the muscle-coupling data.

Sustained motor requirements did not prolong beta-event duration relative to rest, so 'closure elevates the latch' cannot be operationalised as 'closure lengthens a beta event'; it must be a change in burst rate / occupancy.

mapping.source_claim_statement: During sustained isometric contraction, motor beta activity and cortico-muscular beta connectivity are not sustained but occur as short transient bursts; sustained motor demand does not prolong beta-event duration.
mapping.ree_translation: If MECH-445's closure_commit_beta_coupling path 'elevates/binds' the latch via a beta-like signal, the elevation should be read as raised burst rate or coupling-probability/occupancy of the latch-binding signal, not a tonically raised beta level held for the whole commitment epoch.
mapping.mapping_caveat: The study measured cortico-MUSCULAR beta during a peripheral gripping task, not the cortico-cortical or internal latch dynamics MECH-445 concerns; the transient-burst result may not transfer cleanly to a central commitment latch, and REE's latch is an engineered bistable variable, not a beta rhythm. Used here as a constraint on how to read 'elevation', not as a verdict on the mechanism.
mapping.source_context: MEG + EMG in 18 healthy humans performing a sustained isometric grip (gripping) task.

confidence_components.notes: Solid modern empirical methods (single-trial burst analysis, MEG+EMG) lift source quality. Mapping fidelity is moderate: the paper constrains the temporal form of any beta-coupling claim but addresses cortico-muscular, not central commitment, dynamics. Transfer risk is matched to that gap. Net effect on MECH-445 is a calibration constraint, hence mixed/0.5 rather than a confidence-lowering refutation.
